facts.label: Passivo no presente
facts.sub: Use is/are + particípio para explicar como algo é feito: The sauce is heated slowly. Use by só se quiser dizer quem faz.

facts.label: É feito / São feitos
facts.sub: Para o passivo, use is ou are + particípio: The rice is cooked. The potatoes are fried. Use is para uma coisa e are para várias. Fala do processo, não de quem faz.

facts.label: Por
facts.sub: Use by quando precisa dizer quem ou o que faz: The plates are washed by a machine. Em muitas frases isso não é preciso: The soup is made every day.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The passive uses is or are + a past participle.
We always say who does the action.
The sauce is heated is a passive sentence.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The passive uses is or are + a past participle. → Verdadeiro (Yes, like is cooked.)
We always say who does the action. → Falso (Often we do not.)
The sauce is heated is a passive sentence. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

paragraphs: Ana is a new waitress in Seattle. Today she visits the kitchen for the first time. Bo is the cook, and he is proud of his work. Many dishes are made here every day. Ana wants to explain the food to guests. Bo shows her how it works.

“Welcome to the kitchen, Ana. Here the rice is cooked for twenty minutes.” says Bo. “Wow, it smells good. How is the sauce made?” says Ana. “The tomatoes are mixed with garlic, and then the sauce is heated slowly.” says Bo.
